record.original_question: Let G be a finite group and p be a prime. Let Ψp,G be the class function of G which vanishes on all p-singular elements of G and whose value at each p-regular element x of G is the number of p-elements of CG(x). (a) Is it true that Ψp,G is a character of G? (b) If yes, can Ψp,G be afforded by a projective RG-module, where R is a complete discrete valuation ring of characteristic zero such that the field of fractions of R is a splitting field for G and its subgroups, and the residue field R/J(R) is a splitting field of characteristic p for G and its subgroups? It is known that Ψp,G is a character when G ≅ Sn for any positive integer n and any prime p(T. Scharf, J. Algebra, 139, no. 2(1991), 446–457).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite group and let $p$ be a prime. An element of $G$ is called a $p$-element if its order is a power of $p$, and a $p$-regular element if its order is coprime to $p$; an element of $G$ is called $p$-singular if it is not $p$-regular. Define the class function $\Psi_{p,G}\colon G\to\mathbb{Z}$ by
$$\Psi_{p,G}(x)=\begin{cases}\#\{y\in C_G(x):y\text{ is a }p\text{-element}\},&\text{if }x\text{ is }p\text{-regular},\\ 0,&\text{if }x\text{ is }p\text{-singular},\end{cases}$$
where $C_G(x)$ denotes the centralizer of $x$ in $G$.

(a) Is $\Psi_{p,G}$ always a character of $G$ (i.e. the character of some finite-dimensional complex representation of $G$)?

(b) If the answer to (a) is yes, let $R$ be a complete discrete valuation ring of characteristic $0$ whose field of fractions $K$ is a splitting field for $G$ and all of its subgroups, and whose residue field $R/J(R)$ has characteristic $p$ and is a splitting field for $G$ and all of its subgroups. Is $\Psi_{p,G}$ afforded by a projective $RG$-module, i.e. does there exist a finitely generated projective $RG$-module $P$ such that the character of the $KG$-module $K\otimes_R P$ equals $\Psi_{p,G}$?

(It is known that $\Psi_{p,G}$ is a character when $G\cong S_n$ for every positive integer $n$ and every prime $p$.)

status_evidence.title: Scharf, J. Algebra 139 (1991)
status_evidence.snippet: Scharf showed Ψ_{p,G} is a character for G = S_n for all n and all primes p.
status_evidence.claim: The symmetric group case is settled affirmatively.
